First stepA free 15 minute call

Healing starts here

Hi, I'm Dr. Tucker. I work with couples, almost exclusively.

I'm a licensed psychologist and relationship specialist. Every couple that walks in has a pattern. One pursues, one withdraws. One keeps score, one goes quiet. By the second session I can usually name it, and naming it is the first thing that changes.

From there, the method depends on you: Emotionally Focused Therapy, the Gottman Method, or Integrative Behavioral Couples Therapy. All three have real evidence behind them. I'll explain the choice in plain language.

My office is at Elevate Offices in Brownsburg, and a lot of my work happens by video. Under PSYPACT I can see couples in 40+ states, as long as you're both in a member state when we meet.

I don't take insurance, on purpose. It keeps your records yours and our work free of someone else's session limits. You get a superbill after every session, and many clients with out-of-network benefits are reimbursed around half, depending on their plan.

Couples therapy by video, with a psychologist, in 40+ states.

Under PSYPACT, a psychologist licensed in one member state can see clients by video in every other member state. I'm licensed in Indiana and hold the compact's APIT/E.Passport credential (Mobility #16033). The one rule: you and your partner both have to be physically in a participating state at the time of the session.

Not yet: California, New York, Massachusetts, Oregon, Hawaii and New Mexico. Iowa joins in July 2027 and Louisiana in January 2028. Membership changes, so I confirm your state before we schedule.

How a video session works

We meet on a secure, HIPAA-compliant video platform. You can be in the same room or in two different places, as long as both places are in a member state. Sessions are 55 or 90 minutes, same as in person, and the fee is the same: $350 and $525. Superbills go out after each session for out-of-network reimbursement.

When in person makes more sense

Some couples do better in a room, and intensives are almost always in person. My office is at Elevate Offices in Brownsburg, Indiana, twenty minutes west of downtown Indianapolis. Couples can also travel in for half-day and full-day intensives.

Not sure if your state counts? Ask. It takes thirty seconds.

Tell me where you are and what's going on. I'll tell you whether we can work together and how.

Couples therapy online in Illinois, from a psychologist one state east

Chicago has plenty of therapists, but couples specialists with doctoral training are a smaller group, and many keep a waitlist. If you'd rather start soon, or you'd rather not run into your therapist at the grocery store, video is another way to do this.

Free 15 minute consultHow PSYPACT works
WhereChicago, the North Shore, Naperville and Oak Park
Time zoneCentral, one hour behind Indiana
FormatSecure video, 55 or 90 minutes
Fee$350 / $525, superbill provided

Working with Illinois couples

What's different about doing this from Illinois.

We meet by video, usually in the evening, from wherever you both are, as long as that's somewhere in Illinois or another PSYPACT state when the session starts. You can be on one couch or on two laptops in two different rooms.

Illinois is a PSYPACT member, which is what lets me work with you without an Illinois license. My authority comes from the compact and is verifiable by my APIT number.

Insurance and reimbursement in Illinois

I'm a private-pay practice. Many Illinois PPO plans include out-of-network mental health benefits. I'll give you a superbill after every session to submit to your plan. FSA and HSA cards work for the full fee.

The methods

Emotionally Focused Therapy, the Gottman Method and Integrative Behavioral Couples Therapy. Which one we use depends on your pattern, and I'll explain the choice in plain language in the first two sessions. More on how I work with couples.

The one rule
You both have to be in Illinois, or another PSYPACT state, when the session starts.
